commits.message:
fix(ci): repair the release workflow so it can publish a binary

publish.yml has never produced a release with an artefact. The v0.1.0 release
exists with zero assets, the v0.1.1 tag has no release at all, and the workflow
has no recorded successful run. Four independent defects, none of them caused
by the recent action bumps in #330:

- `actions/setup-rust@v2` does not exist (`gh api repos/actions/setup-rust`
  returns 404), so the job failed at that step on every run. Replaced with the
  same `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` action and pin the Lint workflow uses.
- It requested `rust-version: stable`, but `rust-toolchain` at the repository
  root pins nightly-2026-04-16 and takes precedence, so the requested toolchain
  could never have applied. The toolchain is now stated to match that file.
- `::set-output` has been disabled by GitHub, so `steps.tag.outputs.tag_name`
  resolved to an empty string. Use `github.ref_name`, which is already the tag
  name on a tag push, and drop the step entirely.
- The asset path was `cargo-cost-lint/target/release/cargo-cost-lint`, but
  cargo-cost-lint is a workspace member, so its artefacts land in the
  workspace-root `target/`. That directory has never existed. Because
  `fail_on_unmatched_files` defaults to false, the upload matched nothing and
  still reported success — which is how v0.1.0 was published with no assets.

Also: fold the two identical action-gh-release invocations into one, add
`fail_on_unmatched_files: true` so a missing artefact fails loudly, add the
shared rust-cache, and mark tags carrying a pre-release suffix as pre-releases
so a test tag such as v0.0.0-ci-test cannot be presented as the latest stable
release.

Verified locally that `cargo build --release --package cargo-cost-lint`
produces `target/release/cargo-cost-lint`.
